blocks.text: INT-02 · The basic institutional lexicon
Lesson overview

Who reads open Arab sources meets every day names of institutions, offices, acts and titles: ⁧مَجْلِسُ النُّوَّابِ⁩ , ⁧رَئِيسُ الحُكُومَةِ⁩ , ⁧مَرْسُومٌ رِئَاسِيٌّ⁩ , ⁧دَخَلَ حَيِّزَ التَّنْفِيذِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَالِي الوَزِيرِ⁩ . In this unit you learn the basic vocabulary of the State (the three powers, the government and ministries, parliaments, the judiciary in general terms), local administration, official acts and international organizations, with differences between Arab countries and the protocol titles. Above all, learn a rule of method: the names of institutions have an official form and a consolidated translation, which you seek and do not invent. Two weeks.

rows: INT-01; ONO-03 (names of institutions); B1-16 (Political lexicon)
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 150–151), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, institutional sites in Arabic (for the exercise 11), session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. appoint the three powers of the State and their main institutions;
2. to recognise the names of ministries, parliaments and offices, including in the variants of different countries;
3. understand the official acts (law, decree, decision, agreement) and stages of their adoption;
4. understanding and rendering protocolary titles in English ( ⁧فَخَامَة⁩ , ⁧جَلَالَة⁩ , ⁧مَعَالِي⁩ , ⁧سَعَادَة⁩ );
5. translate a brief institutional statement using established translations of names.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: 1. Dialogue 1 · A Moroccan communiqué
In the festival review (INT-01), Luca found a statement from the Moroccan Ministry of Culture (invented) and reads it with Karīm.

rows: ⁧كَرِيمُ، وَجَدْتُ بَلَاغًا مِنْ وِزَارَةِ الثَّقَافَةِ المَغْرِبِيَّةِ عَنِ المِهْرَجَانِ.⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧فِيهِ كَلِمَاتٌ لَا أَعْرِفُهَا.⁩
Luca: KarīmI found a statement from the Moroccan Ministry of Culture about the festival. There are words I don't know.
⁧؟ هٰذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ مَغْرِبِيَّةٌ جِدًّا. فِي المَشْرِقِ يَقُولُونَ عَادَةً⁩ « ⁧بَلَاغ⁩ » ⁧كَرِيم:⁩ ⁧اِقْرَأْ.⁩ .« ⁧بَيَانٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ »
Karīm: «Balāġ»? It's a very Moroccan word. In the Prunuseq they usually say "press communication" . Read it.
Luke: "The head of government has announced... "Why not the prime minister"?

⁧وَفِي⁩ .« ⁧رَئِيسَ الحُكُومَةِ⁩ » ⁧فِي المَغْرِبِ، مُنْذُ دُسْتُورِ ٢٠١١، يُسَمَّى⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧يَخْتَلِفُ⁩ .« ⁧رَئِيسُ مَجْلِسِ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ » ⁧أَوْ⁩ « ⁧رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ » ⁧بُلْدَانٍ أُخْرَى⁩ ⁧المَنْصِبُ قَلِيلًا، وَيَخْتَلِفُ الاِسْمُ أَيْضًا.⁩

Karīm: In Morocco, since the constitution of 2011, is called the Head of Government. In other countries the Prime Minister is either the President of the Council of Ministers. The charge is a little different, and so is the name.
Luke: What about the council of advisors? Counselors of whom?

⁧هُوَ الغُرْفَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ فِي البَرْلَمَانِ المَغْرِبِيِّ، مَعَ مَجْلِسِ النُّوَّابِ. لَا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧تُتَرْجِمْهُ حَرْفِيًّا: هُنَاكَ تَرْجَمَةٌ إِيطَالِيَّةٌ مُعْتَمَدَةٌ فِي المَصَادِرِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ.⁩

Karīm: It is the second chamber of the Moroccan parliament, together with the Chamber of Representatives. Do not translate it to the letter: there is an Italian translation consolidated in official sources.
⁧وَسَيَدْخُلُ القَرَارُ حَيِّزَ التَّنْفِيذِ بَعْدَ نَشْرِهِ فِي⁩ » ⁧وَهٰذِهِ الجُمْلَةُ:⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ .« ⁧الجَرِيدَةِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ⁩
Luca: And this sentence: ...The decision will enter into force after publication in the Official Journal.

⁧يَعْنِي أَنَّ القَرَارَ يُصْبِحُ سَارِيًا. وَالجَرِيدَةُ الرَّسْمِيَّةُ⁩ « ⁧حَيِّزُ التَّنْفِيذِ⁩ » ⁧كَرِيم:⁩ ⁧هِيَ الَّتِي تَنْشُرُ فِيهَا الدَّوْلَةُ قَوَانِينَهَا وَمَرَاسِيمَهَا، مِثْلَ جَرِيدَتِكُمُ⁩ ⁧الرَّسْمِيَّةِ فِي إِيطَالِيَا.⁩
Karīm: «Ḥayyiz at-tanfīḏIt means that the decision becomes effective. And the Official Journal is where the State publishes its laws and decrees, like your Official Gazette in Italy.
⁧إِذَنْ، فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ، أَبْحَثُ عَنِ المُقَابِلِ الإِيطَالِيِّ الرَّسْمِيِّ، لَا عَنِ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧التَّرْجَمَةِ الحَرْفِيَّةِ.⁩
Luke: Then in the translation I look for the official Italian equivalent, not the literal translation.
⁧بِالضَّبْطِ. أَسْمَاءُ المُؤَسَّسَاتِ مِثْلُ أَسْمَاءِ الأَشْخَاصِ: لَهَا شَكْلٌ⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧ثَابِتٌ، وَلَا نَخْتَرِعُهَا.⁩
Karīm: Exactly. The names of institutions are like the names of people: they have a fixed form, and we do not invent them.
Luke: What if I don't find an equivalent?
⁧تَكْتُبُ الاِسْمَ العَرَبِيَّ بِحُرُوفٍ لَاتِينِيَّةٍ، ثُمَّ تَرْجَمَةً بَيْنَ قَوْسَيْنِ.⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧هٰكَذَا يَفْهَمُ القَارِئُ، وَيَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَبْحَثَ عَنِ الأَصْلِ.⁩
Karīm: Write the Arabic name in Latin characters and then a translation in parentheses. So the reader understands and can search for the original.

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧بَلَاغ⁩ (Moroccan use) = ⁧بَيَانٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ (Prunus). ⁧المَنْصِب⁩ The charge shall be: ⁧الغُرْفَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ⁩ The second chamber is the second chamber. ⁧مُعْتَمَد⁩ Consolidated, officially recognised. ⁧سَارٍ⁩ · ⁧سَارِيًا⁩ In force, effective. ⁧لَا نَخْتَرِعُهَا⁩ We don't invent them. ⁧بَيْنَ قَوْسَيْنِ⁩ In parentheses.
2. The three powers
judicial ⁧المَحَاكِمُالسُّلْطَةُ القَضَائِيَّةُ⁩ ⁧المَحْكَمَةُ الدُّسْتُورِيَّةُ⁩ ·

The principle that separates the three powers is called ⁧الفَصْلُ بَيْنَ السُّلُطَاتِ⁩ • the separation of powers. In many texts the ⁧رَقَابَة⁩ The control shall be: ⁧الرَّقَابَةُ البَرْلَمَانِيَّةُ عَلَى الحُكُومَةِ⁩ Parliamentary control over the government is.
3. The Executive: Head of State, Government, Ministries

The head of state. ⁧رَئِيسُ الجُمْهُورِيَّةِ⁩ (Republics) ⁧المَلِكُ⁩ (Monarchies: Morocco, Jordan, Saudi Arabia...) · ⁧الأَمِيرُ⁩ (some Gulf States) · ⁧السُّلْطَانُ⁩ (Oman). Next to the king or the emir: ⁧وَلِيُّ العَهْدِ⁩ The Crown Prince. The government. ⁧الحُكُومَةُ⁩ · ⁧مَجْلِسُ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ The Council of Ministers ⁧رَئِيسُ الوُزَرَاءِ⁩ / ⁧رَئِيسُ الحُكُومَةِ⁩ The Prime Minister / Head of Government ⁧وَزِيرُ دَوْلَةٍ⁩ Minister without portfolio ⁧تَعْدِيلٌ وِزَارِيٌّ⁩ It's a dough. The most frequent ministries.
⁧وِزَارَةُ الأَوْقَافِ⁩ Ministry of Religious Affairs (Lett. () Religious property ()

Names change. The same ministry can be called differently in different countries ( ⁧وِزَارَةُ التَّرْبِيَةِ الوَطَنِيَّةِ⁩ in Morocco, ⁧وِزَارَةُ التَّرْبِيَةِ وَالتَّعْلِيمِ⁩ in Egypt), and governments often change names and competences ( ⁧اِخْتِصَاصَات⁩ ) of ministries. Always check the name on the official website, at the date of the text.
4. Parliaments and the judiciary
Parliaments: some examples. The name of the parliament and its chambers changes from country to country.

The words of parliamentary work: ⁧نَائِب⁩ • Member of the European Parliament (pl. ⁧نُوَّاب⁩ ) · ⁧جَلْسَة⁩ Sitting (B1-16) · ⁧مَشْرُوعُ قَانُونٍ⁩ • draft law • ⁧صَوَّتَ عَلَى⁩ • vote • ⁧أَقَرَّ⁩ • to approve • ⁧صَادَقَ عَلَى⁩ • to ratify, approve definitively • ⁧الأَغْلَبِيَّة⁩ ·
⁧المُعَارَضَة⁩ .

The judiciary (B1-16): ⁧القَضَاء⁩ The judiciary is in the middle of the process. ⁧المَحْكَمَةُ الدُّسْتُورِيَّةُ⁩ The Constitutional Court ⁧مَحْكَمَةُ الاِسْتِئْنَافِ⁩ The Court of Appeal ⁧المَحْكَمَةُ الإِدَارِيَّةُ⁩ The Administrative Court is hereby established. In this course we stop at the names of institutions and the vocabulary of general news.
5. Dialogue 2 · Fakhāma, maʿālī, saʿāda
At the police station, Sāra, the Lebanese interpreter, helps Luca with the titles.

Sāra: Right, but it's betterMaʿālī al-wazīr». For the President of the Republic:Faḫāmat ar-raʾīs». And for the president of the council of ministers, from us:        □Dawlat ar-raʾīs».
Luke: Dawla? Like the Italian State?
⁧سَعَادَةُ⁩ » ⁧الكَلِمَةُ نَفْسُهَا، لٰكِنَّهَا هُنَا لَقَبٌ. وَلِلنَّائِبِ فِي البَرْلَمَانِ:⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ .« ⁧سَعَادَةُ السَّفِيرِ⁩ » ⁧وَلِلسَّفِيرِ أَيْضًا:⁩ .« ⁧النَّائِبِ⁩

Luke: What about kings and princes?
⁧لِلْأَمِيرِ أَوْ لِوَلِيِّ العَهْدِ. وَهٰذِهِ⁩ « ⁧صَاحِبُ السُّمُوِّ⁩ » ⁧، وَ⁩ « ⁧جَلَالَةُ المَلِكِ⁩ » ⁧سَارَة:⁩ ⁧الأَلْقَابُ تَظْهَرُ كَثِيرًا فِي الأَخْبَارِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ.⁩
Sāra: «Ǧalālat al-malikṢāḥib as-sumuww . for a prince or the Crown Prince. These titles often appear in official news.
⁧؟⁩ « ⁧اسْتَقْبَلَ فَخَامَةُ الرَّئِيسِ مَعَالِيَ الوَزِيرِ⁩ » ⁧إِذَنْ كَيْفَ أُتَرْجِمُ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩

⁧عَادَةً.⁩

blocks.text: ⁧نَعَمْ، إِلَّا فِي الرَّسَائِلِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ: هُنَاكَ اللَّقَبُ ضَرُورِيٌّ.⁩ : ⁧سَارَة⁩ Sāra: Yes, except in official letters: there the title is necessary.

What to notice. ⁧تُخَاطِبُ⁩ (III of ⁧خ ط ب⁩ ). ⁧لَقَب⁩ "Titolo" (pl. ⁧أَلْقَاب⁩ ). Titles are names in iḍāfa with charge: ⁧مَعَالِي الوَزِيرِ⁩ , ⁧فَخَامَةُ الرَّئِيسِ⁩ , ⁧سَعَادَةُ السَّفِيرِ⁩ . ⁧مَعَالِي⁩ is indeclinable (always ends in -ī): ⁧اِسْتَقْبَلَ مَعَالِيَ الوَزِيرِ⁩ is written with the -ya to the accusative, but often pronounced maʿālī.
6. Official acts

rows: the Head of State or the Government
a minister, an institution, a court

blocks.text: ⁧بَلَاغ⁩ · ⁧بَيَانٌ صَحَفِيٌّ⁩ press release any institution

The stages. ⁧اِقْتَرَحَ⁩ • propose → ⁧نَاقَشَ⁩ • discuss → ⁧صَوَّتَ عَلَى⁩ • vote → ⁧أَقَرَّ⁩ / ⁧صَادَقَ عَلَى⁩ • approve, ratify → ⁧أَصْدَرَ⁩ • issue → ⁧نُشِرَ فِي الجَرِيدَةِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ⁩ It has been published in the Official Journal → ⁧دَخَلَ حَيِّزَ التَّنْفِيذِ⁩ It has entered into force. And then: ⁧عَدَّلَ⁩ - amend ( ⁧تَعْدِيل⁩ ) · ⁧أَلْغَى⁩ • repeal, cancel ⁧إِلْغَاء⁩ ).
7. Local administration

⁧عَمَالَة⁩ Prefecture (Morocco) ⁧عَامِل⁩ Governor (Morocco) ⁧جَمَاعَة⁩ Common (Morocco) · ⁧قَضَاء⁩ here: District (Lebanon) ⁧قَائِمَقَام⁩ "Chief of the District" is replaced by the following: Beware of false friends. ⁧قَضَاء⁩ in Lebanon it is also an administrative unit, not only the judiciary, ⁧عَامِل⁩ in Morocco, he is a senior official, not a worker; ⁧جَمَاعَة⁩ Morocco is the municipality. The context (and the country of the source) decides.
8. International and regional organisations

rows: The United Nations - General Assembly · Security Council
the European Union · the African Union
The International Monetary Fund - the World Bank

blocks.text: ⁧المَبْعُوثُ الخَاصُّ⁩ · ⁧القُنْصُلِيَّةُ⁩ · ⁧السِّفَارَةُ⁩ the embassy · the consulate · the special envoy

The acronyms. In Arabic the acronyms are used little; organizations appear with the full name for the first time, then in a short form ( ⁧المُنَظَّمَة⁩ , ⁧الجَامِعَة⁩ , ⁧الصُّنْدُوق⁩ ). In the Italian translation he uses the current acronym (UN, WHO, IMF) after the first mention.
9. Titles of the Protocol

rows: His Majesty the King · (journalistic) the King
the President of the Council (Lebanon and other Levant countries)

blocks.text: Translate the titles. In a news or review in English the titles are almost always omitted; in an official letter (B1-22) Italian equivalents are used (---------------------------------------------------------------------- In an Arabic text, the presence or absence of the title is a clue to the registry and source type (an official agency uses all titles; an independent site often not).
10. Pronunciation

The iḍāfa long institutional names. They read as one word, without internal pauses: wizāratu š-šuʾūni l-ḫāriǧiyya · al-maǧlisu š-šaʿbiyyu l-waṭaniyy. Only the last word takes a break. Titles. faḫāmatu r-raʾīs, ǧalālatu l-malik: la tāʾ marbūṭa of the title is pronounced -t because it is in iḍāfa.
11. New lexicon

rows: ⁧دَخَلَ حَيِّزَ التَّنْفِيذِ⁩ It has entered into force on 1 January 2017 and is therefore not applicable on the date of its entry into force.

blocks.text: Notes of use. ⁧صَادَقَ عَلَى⁩ and ⁧أَقَرَّ⁩ : both approve the text; ⁧صَادَقَ⁩ is often the final ratification (of a treaty, or of a law by another instance). ⁧اِخْتِصَاص⁩ appears in formulas as ⁧هٰذَا لَيْسَ مِنِ اخْتِصَاصِ الوِزَارَةِ⁩ This is not the responsibility of the Ministry. ⁧مَعَالِي⁩ , ⁧فَخَامَة⁩ , ⁧جَلَالَة⁩ do not translate word by word in journalistic texts (section 9).
12. Examples in context
